## **CLIENT DISCOVERY CALL**

Invited [ifeoma@mycityapp.io](mailto:ifeoma@mycityapp.io) [cynthia@mycityapp.io](mailto:cynthia@mycityapp.io) [JBS Praxis](mailto:praxisjbs@gmail.com) [etudor@mycityapp.io](mailto:etudor@mycityapp.io) [tom.asaah@jbspraxis.com](mailto:tom.asaah@jbspraxis.com) [tomblakeasaah@gmail.com](mailto:tomblakeasaah@gmail.com) [bode@mycityapp.io](mailto:bode@mycityapp.io)

Attachments [CLIENT DISCOVERY CALL](https://calendar.google.com/calendar/event?eid=MzVtdjRtdXNocGswMDBza2wydHQ3N2tidHMgcHJheGlzamJzQG0)

Meeting records [Transcript](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1zIHguefwZ1GJ3yXpJYOAhI6vGs-D2We4g2KpSQxQ0fU/edit?usp=drive_web&tab=t.mc9nl95i21hu) 

### **Summary**

The platform capabilities were demonstrated, covering system architecture, human resources, and business operations, resulting in requested customizations.

**Platform Architecture and Functionality**  
The demonstration showcased a centralized dashboard for business intelligence, task management, and sales tracking. Artificial Intelligence analytics and role-based access control provide data-driven oversight and security.

**Human Resources Management Features**  
Discussion focused on automating candidate evaluation, performance reviews, and payroll processing. Disciplinary workflows and configurable employee portals were identified as essential features for operational efficiency.

**Integration and System Customization**  
Decision made to incorporate existing spreadsheet trackers into the platform to centralize partnership management and expense reporting. This integration facilitates the transition from manual files to automated processes.

### **Decisions**

## **Aligned**

* **Secondary assessment platform creation** A second platform will be created to manage candidate applications and assessment submissions separately from the careers page.  
* **Documentation step integration** A formal documentation step is established to be completed prior to the official onboarding process.  
* **Social media vacancy posting method** Vacancy sharing on social media will be handled via links rather than direct platform integration due to the complexity of the build.  
* **Renaming HR dashboard** The "My HR" module is renamed to "Employee Self-Service" (ESS) to improve clarity for the user base.

### **Next steps**

- [ ] \[Cynthia Osakunih\] Outline Operations: Outline the operations flow and structure for human capital management to identify integration requirements.  
- [ ] \[Cynthia Osakunih\] Compile Questions: Compile and present specific questions regarding the system capabilities and support requirements.  
- [ ] \[Cynthia Osakunih\] Gather Team Feedback: Compile feedback from team members regarding the platform and system requirements.  
- [ ] \[Cynthia Osakunih\] Share Excel Sheets: Send the currently used Excel files to Tom-Blake Asaah for system integration analysis.  
- [ ] \[JBS Praxis\] Draft Client Email: Detail the project milestones and current status in an email for Mr. Kish.  
- [ ] \[JBS Praxis\] Review Project Status: Verify all completed parts of the project to confirm technical understanding.  
- [ ] \[JBS Praxis\] Share Draft Email: Send the prepared message to Tom-Blake Asaah for final review before dispatch.

### **Details**

* **Meeting Introductions and Objectives**: Attendees introduced themselves: Tom-Blake Asaah (Founder and Managing Partner of JBS Praxis), Oyebode Oluwasanmi, and Cynthia Osakunih (Operations and People Lead for MyCity App). Tom-Blake Asaah explained that the focus of the meeting is on operations management, human capital management, and system integration, following a previous discovery meeting between JBS Praxis and Oyebode Oluwasanmi ([00:01:21](#00:01:21)).  
* **System Overview and Business Intelligence**: Tom-Blake Asaah provided a demonstration of a software system built for two brands (Fedlinin Hair and Pixie Girl Global), showcasing a command center that functions as a central hub. The dashboard allows users to monitor business performance, including revenue, order volume, average order value, new customer acquisition metrics, and financial status (income versus expenses). The system tracks receivables by aging categories (e.g., 1-30 days, 31-60 days) and provides a secure, device-specific activity log to track user actions ([00:06:47](#00:06:47)).  
  ![][image1]  
* **Task Management and Human Resources Workspace**: Tom-Blake Asaah demonstrated a Kanban-style workspace board for assigning tasks, tracking progress, and managing internal calendars. Within the "My Human Resources" module, employees can access their profiles, clock in and out, view payroll information, see leave days, and respond to system-generated queries regarding attendance or device usage. The system uses device enrollment to verify location and maintain security standards ([00:11:16](#00:11:16)).  
  ![][image2]  
* **Sales, Marketing, and Customer Relationship Management Functionality**: The system includes a sales module that tracks orders, manages product stock, and integrates with payment gateways like Flutterwave and Paystack. A Customer Relationship Management module organizes client data, identifies customer milestones (e.g., birthdays), and supports automated marketing campaigns via templates. Invoicing and logistics are also managed through the platform, allowing users to send invoices, track deliveries, and trigger automated notifications upon delivery ([00:15:29](#00:15:29)).  
  ![][image3]  
* **Artificial Intelligence-Powered Business Analytics**: Tom-Blake Asaah presented an Artificial Intelligence component that enables users to query business data conversationally (e.g., asking about employee costs or payroll status). The Artificial Intelligence utilizes different models—the retriever, the call, and the call action models—to navigate the database and provide specific insights or guidance on system navigation, such as finding the correct module to create coupon codes ([00:21:01](#00:21:01)).  
  ![][image4]  
* **System Administration and Customization**: Users can customize business settings, including branding, policies, and appearance (colors and layout) without writing code. Sensitive information, such as Corporate Affairs Commission registration numbers or Tax Identification Numbers, is stored with encryption, requiring an administrator password to view ([00:23:19](#00:23:19)).  
* **Financial Accounting and Expense Reporting**: The system supports standard accounting practices, including journal entries, a four-column trial balance, Profit and Loss statements, and balance sheets. It allows for bank reconciliation through manual import or application programming interface integration. An expense management feature utilizes artificial intelligence to categorize receipts uploaded by users, posting them directly to the general ledger ([00:25:26](#00:25:26)).  
  ![][image5]  
* **Human Resources and Performance Management**: The Human Resources module centralizes staff directory details, leave approvals, and attendance monitoring. It features a query system for disciplinary issues or policy violations. Managers can set performance targets for employees, which appear on the employees' dashboards, and utilize a reward system to automate bonus calculations based on defined rules ([00:28:52](#00:28:52)).  
  ![][image6]  
* **Recruitment and Candidate Management**: Tom-Blake Asaah showcased the recruitment workflow, which allows users to create new vacancies, publish them to a careers portal, and track applicants. The system uses artificial intelligence to score candidates based on their curriculum vitae and responses (e.g., an 89% or 97% match). Additionally, the system generates interview questions and provides tools for offer management, including electronic signature collection for employment agreements ([00:32:03](#00:32:03)).  
  ![][image7]  
* **Human Resources Analytics and Configuration**: The system allows for the tracking of Key Performance Indicators such as headcount, attrition, and punctuality. Configuration options include geolocation settings for office clock-in radii, salary processing rules (including pension and National Housing Fund contributions), and onboarding content management to display articles for new hires ([00:37:17](#00:37:17)).  
  ![][image8]  
* **Centralized Communication Module**: The platform integrates email, WhatsApp, and Instagram into a single interface. Users can view client communication history, lifetime value, and previous interactions directly within the system. This centralizes external communication, enabling responses without leaving the platform ([00:41:11](#00:41:11)).  
  ![][image9]  
* **Role-Based Access Control and Artificial Intelligence Spend Limits**: Tom-Blake Asaah demonstrated that the system enforces Role-Based Access Control, allowing administrators to restrict access to specific modules (e.g., hiding Sales from the Chief Operating Officer). Users can also set caps on Artificial Intelligence usage costs (e.g., 80,000 units) to control expenses ([00:45:09](#00:45:09)).  
  ![][image10]  
* **Website Management and Clocking Functionality**: The system includes a website builder that allows users to edit content, text, pop-ups, and navigation pages. Additionally, the clocking-in feature verifies location and device authorization, with notifications that can be pushed to email if a user fails to clock in properly ([00:48:23](#00:48:23)).  
  ![][image11]  
* **Feedback on System Demo**: Cynthia Osakunih requested to see the front-end interface, confirming that the demonstration was a sample that could be customized for MyCity App. Discussion confirmed that the system supports reporting dashboards, location-based clocking, and general staff communication platforms ([00:51:26](#00:51:26)).  
  ![][image12]  
* **Task Assignment and Productivity Tracking**: Cynthia Osakunih inquired about task visibility and productivity tracking. Tom-Blake Asaah explained that managers have oversight of all tasks through a Kanban board, which displays items in columns such as "To-Do," "In Progress," "In Review," and "Done." This ensures managers can monitor employee progress and status on assigned work ([00:54:10](#00:54:10)).  
* **Disciplinary and Query Framework**: Cynthia Osakunih discussed the need for structured consequence management beyond just salary deductions. Tom-Blake Asaah confirmed that the system can be configured to handle disciplinary chains (e.g., warnings to suspension) based on company-specific rules and that query automation can be adjusted for leniency (e.g., only flagging third-time offenders) ([00:56:41](#00:56:41)).  
  ![][image13]  
* **Interview Panel Assessment**: Cynthia Osakunih asked about multi-panelist interview assessments. Tom-Blake Asaah clarified that the system allows for setting multiple reviewers, ensuring that each panelist can provide their own ratings and internal notes privately without seeing other reviewers' assessments, which are then consolidated by the hiring manager ([00:58:37](#00:58:37)).  
  ![][image14]  
* **Recruitment Assessments and Process Flow**: Cynthia Osakunih requested clarity on whether the system handles end-to-end recruitment, including psychometric testing and technical case studies. Tom-Blake Asaah confirmed the capability to build these features and proposed a two-platform approach: one for carrier management and offers, and a second platform where candidates can apply, take tests, and receive results ([01:00:58](#01:00:58)).  
  ![][image15]  
* **Offer Generation and Digital Acceptance**: Tom-Blake Asaah demonstrated how candidates are moved from a shortlisted status to an offered status, which triggers the generation of an offer letter ([01:03:18](#01:03:18)). The system allows for offer letters to be sent via email, where they expire in 15 days, and candidates can sign them electronically using their devices ([01:04:15](#01:04:15)). Once signed, the offer status updates automatically on the platform, and the documents become locked ([01:05:12](#01:05:12)).  
  ![][image16]  
* **Onboarding Documentation and Social Media Integration**: Cynthia Osakunih requested that a formal documentation step be added prior to the official onboarding phase, to which Tom-Blake Asaah agreed. Regarding posting vacancies to social media platforms like LinkedIn, Tom-Blake Asaah noted that while it is possible, it is a "heavy build," and suggested that simply copying and pasting the link from the system is a viable alternative ([01:06:08](#01:06:08)).  
  ![][image17]  
* **Payroll Statutory Deductions**: Cynthia Osakunih inquired about the system’s ability to manage scaling payroll needs, specifically regarding statutory deductions like Industrial Training Fund (ITF) and Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF). Tom-Blake Asaah confirmed the system can handle full-fledged payroll, including automatic tax deductions and statutory reporting, once the relevant features are toggled on in the system ([01:06:51](#01:06:51)).  
  ![][image18]  
* **Employee Self-Service Dashboard**: Cynthia Osakunih requested that the "My HR" section be renamed to "Employee Self-Service" (ESS) to better reflect its function, where employees can update personal records, view daily tasks, access calendars, and see assigned tags. Tom-Blake Asaah agreed that the system is fully customizable and could be renamed accordingly ([01:07:35](#01:07:35)).  
* **System Notifications and Performance Management**: Cynthia Osakunih asked about automated email prompts for approvals, such as leave requests, confirmation letters, and invoices. Tom-Blake Asaah confirmed that the email system can be configured for sensitive notifications and that the performance management module allows for setting specific KPIs per role, adding new KPIs, and conducting reviews by line managers or designated individuals ([01:08:22](#01:08:22)).  
  ![][image19]  
* **Partnership Pipeline and Proposal Management**: Cynthia Osakunih discussed the need for a tracker to manage partnership pipelines, noting current usage of Excel sheets to track leads from ongoing to closed status. Tom-Blake Asaah showed the CRM functionality, which allows users to move leads across different stages of a sales pipeline ([01:10:41](#01:10:41)). Additionally, they confirmed that the system supports automated proposal and Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) management, which can be sent to clients or downloaded as PDF documents ([01:11:35](#01:11:35)).  
  ![][image20]  
* **Integration of Existing Excel Trackers**: Regarding the transition from existing Excel-based trackers to the new system, Cynthia Osakunih expressed that it should be straightforward to develop these modules. Tom-Blake Asaah agreed and requested that Cynthia Osakunih provide the current Excel sheets to facilitate the integration and full automation of these processes ([01:12:56](#01:12:56)).  
  ![][image21]  
* **Expense Management and Reporting**: Cynthia Osakunih inquired about handling expense requests, approval workflows, and reporting against actual expenditures ([01:12:56](#01:12:56)). Tom-Blake Asaah explained that the system allows employees to request cash, which then routes through a set approval workflow—customizable by hierarchy—before reaching the disbursement stage, where bank transaction details are recorded ([01:13:39](#01:13:39)).  
  ![][image22]  
* **Meeting Conclusion and Documentation Requirements**: Cynthia Osakunih concluded their portion of the meeting, stating they would need to coordinate with the rest of their team to provide further details and gather necessary documents. Tom-Blake Asaah noted that moving forward would involve an NDA and a review of the existing Excel sheets to ensure full automation ([01:14:49](#01:14:49)).  
* **Post-Meeting Internal Review and Tasking**: Following the client's departure, Tom-Blake Asaah and JBS Praxis reflected on the complexity of the project, noting the significant amount of work required ([01:15:44](#01:15:44)). Tom-Blake Asaah assigned JBS Praxis the task of drafting an email to Mr. Kish, outlining the project milestones and offering a walkthrough of the completed work, which JBS Praxis committed to preparing ([01:16:54](#01:16:54)).
